back2basics.concept: Consumer Price Index and Inflation Targeting
back2basics.text: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures retail inflation by tracking price changes in a basket of goods and services consumed by households. The Reserve Bank of India uses inflation targeting, aiming for a 4% inflation rate with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%, to maintain price stability and support economic growth. When inflation crosses this band, the RBI adjusts monetary policy, such as changing the repo rate, to control inflationary pressures.

2026-11-13-am-19e14e5238.deck: Retail inflation in India rose to 6.1% in October 2026, crossing the Reserve Bank of India’s upper tolerance limit of 6% for the first time in two years. This rise, driven mainly by food and fuel prices, has implications for monetary policy and cost of living, making it relevant for UPSC aspirants studying the economy.

back2basics.concept: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)
back2basics.text: The CAG is a constitutional authority responsible for auditing government expenditure and ensuring accountability. It conducts audits of various government departments and programmes to assess financial propriety and performance. Traditionally, audits were sector-specific, but integrated audits combine related sectors to provide a broader view of outcomes.

back2basics.patternId: Digital public infrastructure and AI governance
back2basics.text: Cybersecurity involves protecting digital financial infrastructure from unauthorized access and fraud. Payment systems use APIs and automated processes to facilitate transactions, which require robust security to prevent exploitation. Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) are methods to identify and fix security weaknesses. Real-time fraud detection systems monitor transactions to detect suspicious patterns and prevent financial losses.

2026-11-13-am-97a412ee03.deck: The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau (TGCSB) warned NBFCs, fintech platforms, and banks about increasing AI-assisted cyberattacks targeting payment and loan disbursement systems. This alert is crucial for UPSC aspirants to understand cybersecurity threats in the financial sector and the regulatory responses to protect digital payment infrastructure.

structure.intro: AI-assisted cyberattacks are emerging threats to financial payment systems, exploiting vulnerabilities to commit fraud.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the TGCSB advisory on AI-assisted cyberattacks:

Which of the statements is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because institutions should resume automation only after cybersecurity teams have tested and patched vulnerabilities.

body.label: Targeted institutions
body.text: Smaller NBFCs with weaker cybersecurity systems are primarily targeted by fraudsters using AI-assisted cyberattacks.

body.label: Attack methodology
body.text: Attackers study internal processes for 10 to 12 days to identify vulnerabilities like whitelisted IDs and payment API credentials, then exploit these to make fraudulent requests appear genuine.

body.label: Fraud techniques
body.text: Automated scripts initiate payout requests outside normal batch windows, split payments into smaller amounts, and rapidly transfer money through mule accounts to evade detection.

sections.heading: What are the AI-assisted cyber threats to payment systems?

body.label: Proactive security focus
body.text: Financial institutions should prevent fraud at the source by detecting suspicious activity in real time and disrupting fund movement through mule accounts.

body.label: Technical safeguards
body.text: Institutions are advised to conduct regular Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT), secure payment APIs, deploy real-time fraud detection, and implement transaction velocity checks and limits.

body.label: Response protocols
body.text: In case of an attack, institutions should switch to manual operations, freeze accounts, clear pending API calls, and resume automation only after patching vulnerabilities.

sections.heading: What preventive measures has TGCSB recommended?

body.label: Immediate reporting
body.text: Suspected fraud must be reported immediately via the 1930 helpline, the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, CERT-In within six hours, and the RBI through the DAKSH portal.

body.label: Coordination
body.text: Institutions should alert beneficiary banks and the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) to coordinate responses.

body.label: Record keeping
body.text: Complete records of all high-risk payouts should be maintained for investigation and audit.

sections.heading: How should institutions report and respond to cyber incidents?

body.label: Joint Ministerial Statement

body.text: The meeting welcomed initiatives including the BIMSTEC Regional Centre of Excellence for Public Health in Sri Lanka, the Centre of Excellence on Tropical Medicine in Thailand, and India’s commitment to host a Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine at ITRA, Jamnagar.

body.text: India highlighted its progress towards Universal Health Coverage, including over 1.85 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs and the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana covering over 60 crore people with cashless hospitalisation up to ₹5 lakh.

body.label: Digital Health Initiatives
body.text: India’s National Telemedicine Service, eSanjeevani, has crossed 50 crore teleconsultations, and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission is building an interoperable digital health ecosystem.

body.label: Traditional Medicine Centre
body.text: India committed to hosting the BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine at ITRA, Jamnagar, to promote research, academic exchange, and preservation of traditional knowledge.

body.label: Deepening Bilateral Relations
body.text: India’s bilateral engagements with Sri Lanka and Nepal during the meeting reinforce longstanding partnerships and support regional prosperity and stability.

body.label: Supporting Inclusive Development

back2basics.concept: Conference of Parties (COP) and Paris Agreement
back2basics.text: The Conference of Parties (COP) is the supreme decision-making body of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), where countries negotiate and review progress on climate action. The Paris Agreement is an international treaty aiming to limit global temperature rise to well below 2°C, preferably 1.5°C, through nationally determined contributions by countries. The COP meetings assess commitments, finance, and scientific progress to guide global climate policy.

2026-11-13-am-e0bd5a98d9.deck: The 31st Conference of Parties (COP31) began in Antalya, Türkiye, focusing on delivering past climate finance commitments and assessing progress under the Paris Agreement. UPSC aspirants should understand the ongoing challenges in international climate negotiations, finance, and India’s stance on climate targets.

body.label: Focus on past commitments
body.text: COP31 prioritizes delivering on existing commitments like providing $300 billion annually by 2035 and tripling adaptation finance, rather than setting new ambitious targets.

body.label: Climate finance challenges
body.text: Practical mechanisms for climate fund flows have been deferred to COP32, reflecting difficulties in mobilizing and distributing promised funds.

body.label: Global stocktake initiation
body.text: The second global stocktake under the Paris Agreement begins at COP31 to assess collective progress on climate goals.

body.label: Scientific input delays
body.text: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has delayed timelines for new reports that inform policy acceleration to limit temperature rise.

body.label: Voluntary fossil fuel roadmap
body.text: Unlike COP28, COP31 lacks a formal roadmap to phase out fossil fuels; a voluntary roadmap exists but is not part of official negotiations.

sections.heading: What are the main issues at COP31?

body.label: India’s stance on electrification target
body.text: India refused to endorse the COP31 electrification target to increase electricity’s share from 23% to 35% by 2035, demanding predictable finance, technology transfer, and respect for nationally determined mitigation approaches.

body.label: Vulnerability of small island nations
body.text: Ministerial visits to Fiji and Tuvalu before COP31 highlighted the urgency for vulnerable nations threatened by rising temperatures.

body.label: Funding shortfalls
body.text: The recent approval of $21 million from the Loss and Damage fund to Nepal, far below the billions requested, illustrates the funding gap.

body.label: Geopolitical and financial tensions
body.text: Global conflicts, the US withdrawal from the Paris Agreement, and financial strains in Europe complicate consensus and fund mobilization.

back2basics.text: Electoral rolls are official lists of eligible voters maintained by the Election Commission.
